articles.title: The Star Rail field manual
articles.summary: Find a workflow, learn a mechanic or look up an individual control.

sections.title: Find an answer
paragraphs: Open the Star Rail rocket on the left rail, then choose Help Documentation below the other tools. The grouped Contents follows the game workflow. The A–Z Index includes both guides and individual fields and controls. Search reads the entire manual and reference, including related terms, shorthand and small spelling mistakes.

Every keyword narrows your search. Try “alt ult”, “pet range”, “HP cost”, “memosprite dots”, “art” or “aha crit”. Selecting a field result opens its guide and scrolls directly to that reference. Back retraces visited guides and index pages. Press / to focus search; Escape clears an active search.

sections.title: Learn in context
paragraphs: Hover a control, label, image, menu entry or preview to see its explanation. Keyboard focus also opens hover help. Numeric controls show their limits and units where defined; checkboxes report their current state, and disabled controls explain their requirements. Escape, scrolling or dragging dismisses the tooltip.

The same field reference supplies the manual and tooltips. Dynamic ability rows and refreshed combat panels receive help when rendered. A contextual ? Help button opens the relevant guide. Reading help does not change configuration, spend a resource, send a message or advance combat.

sections.title: What this manual covers
paragraphs: Character GM settings, Energy, standard and alternate Ultimates, enhanced forms, skills, HP requirements, summons, combat, Toughness, Break, Aha, Light Cones, DoT, artwork, the phone hub, Messenger, missions, crafting and Eidolons are covered here. Memosprites are supplied by a separate addon; its supported configuration is documented alongside its integration.

Images are bundled with the module and can be expanded to inspect labels. The manual needs no external documentation service. GM-only game actions retain their existing permission checks; opening their explanations does not grant access.

articles.title: GM setup: first character to first combat
articles.summary: Configure a complete kit and verify it in a small encounter.

sections.title: Prepare a character
paragraphs: Enable Ultimates for the world, use a supported D&D5e character Actor, and give its player ownership. Place its token on a scene before testing map-dependent abilities. Configure reusable Elements and Paths first so each character can refer to stable IDs.
steps: Open the character sheet’s HSR Settings as GM. Choose Element, Path and party membership.
In Ultimates, enable the system, set Maximum Energy and either configure standard artwork/text or enable an alternate Ultimate.
In Abilities, enable the Skill, choose its SP cost, and add HP requirements or an Actor summon list if needed.
Configure enhanced abilities independently if the kit has an enhanced form.
Set shared Skill and Technique Points in their configuration menus, then show the desired widgets.
Add a character and test enemy to initiative. Test readiness, chat text, costs, placement and completion.

sections.title: Run a controlled check
paragraphs: Set enough charge/SP to cast once. A successful Skill posts its description and pays its configured costs. An Ultimate uses its active form’s charge system, shows its splash and runs its optional code. If an off-turn Ultimate inserts a temporary participant, finish it with the completion flow and confirm the original turn resumes.

For a summon, test one creature that fits and one that cannot. Confirm the full footprint stays inside the range and respects lighting-blocking walls. A cancelled or impossible placement must leave costs unspent or restore a queued reservation.

sections.title: Before players rely on it
paragraphs: Verify images load for another connected client, not just the GM. Check ownership, selected main character and party flags separately. Descriptive text explains the kit; unsupported mechanics in prose need an explicit item workflow or deliberate automation. A separate companion addon must be enabled before its own configuration tab can appear.

articles.title: Player workflow and ownership
articles.summary: Select your main character, use abilities and finish temporary turns.

sections.title: Choose and show your character
paragraphs: Main Character selection tells the module which owned character your personal widgets and phone actions should prioritize. Ownership permits using an Actor; selection and Main Party membership are separate. A GM Party Override can lock membership against player selection changes.

Show the combat HUD or ability bubbles from the Star Rail/phone controls. Closing a local widget hides its display and does not disable the underlying ability. Drag grips and resize handles change your local arrangement.

sections.title: Use the normal ability flow
paragraphs: Skills check the shared SP balance, optional actual-HP cost and any creature placement. Ultimates check the active form’s Energy or alternate components. Techniques use their separate shared resource outside initiative. Unsupported or unauthorized casts are rejected before they become legitimate extra casts.

A connected active GM is required for player requests that need authority. If a button is unavailable, inspect charge, combat state, ownership and active form. Repeated clicks while an ability resolves do not bypass its lock.

sections.title: Complete the action
paragraphs: Resolve the chat card’s instructions and supported damage controls. Complete Ultimate and Complete Elation Action remove the corresponding temporary participant and resume initiative. A chat description does not automatically implement every effect written in prose.

articles.title: Left rail and Star Rail menus
articles.summary: Know which menu opens configuration, live combat tools or player apps.

sections.title: The left rail
paragraphs: The rocket groups the Star Rail tools. The GM rail keeps its compact Hub, Battle Pass and DM Combat entries, followed by Help Documentation. Player-visible tools and their permissions differ, but Help stays last and is available to both roles.
HSR Hub opens the phone-style launcher. DM Combat opens the encounter panel. Battle Pass requires its separate module. Help opens this manual; it never starts an encounter action.

sections.title: Configuration and live controls
paragraphs: The GM Panel provides live shared resources and per-character tuning, plus launchers for specialized editors. Character HSR Settings belongs to one Actor. DM Combat focuses on the current encounter. The Phone Hub Designer changes launcher layout and artwork; its preview does not activate a live phone action.

Menu buttons can open missions, crafting, Messenger, equipment tools and character selection. A GM-only destination keeps its ordinary restrictions even if a player can read its documentation. An unavailable addon should be enabled before trying its launcher.

articles.title: Character settings: menus, search and saving
articles.summary: Use grouped settings and related-keyword filtering without losing configuration.

sections.title: Six related menus
paragraphs: Character contains membership, identity and Element/Path controls. Ultimates contains Energy, charge mode and Ultimate effects. Abilities contains Skill, Talent, Technique and Elation settings. Enhanced Form groups stance behavior and replacement abilities. Artwork groups portraits, orb/splash art and cropping. Combat contains Break, Toughness and boss behavior.

Find a setting searches labels, field identifiers, hints and related words. “alt” and “alt ult” find Alternate Ultimate. “art” finds image-related controls, including portraits, icons, splash art and token skin. Multiple words must all match; results hide unrelated settings rather than merely highlighting everything.

sections.title: Scope and expansion
paragraphs: All menus searches the character’s full configuration; This menu limits the search to the selected page. Clear removes the filter. Expand sections opens the collapsible groups. Choosing another menu while searching adjusts the scope to that menu.

A filter changes the view, not the Actor’s configuration. Hidden fields keep their values. Alternate mode switches save immediately. The regular sheet’s existing autosave behavior still applies; dedicated designers have their own Save action. A preview or search is not a cast.

sections.title: Know the meaning of a value
paragraphs: Read the field’s tooltip for units and whether it changes a live value, draft or display. Current Energy is not Maximum Energy; an orb image is not a splash image; shared SP is not the per-character Skill cost. Use the reference links to distinguish similarly named fields.

articles.title: Party membership, selection and rewards
articles.summary: Main Party, GM overrides, trial labels and reward eligibility are separate switches.

sections.title: Main Party and selection
paragraphs: Main Party influences allied-turn waiting for queued Ultimates. A player selecting an owned main character requests synchronized membership; GM Party Override prevents that selector from changing a locked Actor’s status. A GM-controlled character can be managed directly in the GM Panel.
Trial Character adds a red Trial label to its combat HUD orb. This is presentation and does not grant ownership, charge or extra turns.

sections.title: Rewards
paragraphs: Mission assignment identifies the intended recipients. Characters with non-GM owners and GM-controlled characters explicitly marked Receives Rewards can be eligible. Owning, selecting, assigning and receiving rewards are different concepts. Inspect the assignment list before distributing a mission’s Items.
Receives Rewards does not itself grant an Item. Main Party membership does not turn a hidden mission public. Use each campaign app’s own visibility and reward controls.

articles.title: Elements and Paths
articles.summary: Maintain reusable catalogs and stable character assignments.

sections.title: Reusable definitions
paragraphs: Element Manager defines display name, stable ID, icon and charge/ready colors. Path Manager defines a name, ID, icon and Path color. Characters select from these catalogs. An Element’s ID is used for weakness matching and related automation, while its icon and colors affect presentation.

Use Foundry-accessible icon paths. Renaming a display label is different from changing an ID that existing Actors or effects reference. Check existing assignments before removing or changing identifiers.

sections.title: Mechanical connections
paragraphs: The selected Element participates in Toughness weaknesses and relevant Light Cone checks. A Path can determine eligibility for Path-specific effects, such as the configured Elation Path. Selecting a label does not automatically create a class, subclass or spell list.

Memosprite availability is controlled by the installed companion addon. Reading its guide does not change an older addon’s Path restrictions. Skill and Ultimate Actor summons in this module have no Path restriction.

articles.title: Energy and the REGEN ability score
articles.summary: Set charge capacity, automatic gains and the after-Ultimate round lock.

sections.title: Current, maximum and regeneration
paragraphs: Current Energy is stored charge. Maximum Energy is the threshold needed for a standard Ultimate. The Energy Regen score uses floor((score − 10) / 2), like an ordinary ability modifier. The added REGEN card on the sheet edits this same score.

Configured attack, being-hit and ability-related Energy awards use the module’s normal event flow and regeneration rules. They are not extra guaranteed awards for each line of descriptive text. The score is clamped to 1–30.

sections.title: Active charge mode
paragraphs: A standard Ultimate becomes ready when Current reaches Maximum. Casting consumes its charge. When the active form uses an alternate Ultimate, all alternate components must be lit and positive standard Energy gains are blocked. The ordinary Energy pool is retained separately.

Set Energy in the sheet is an explicit current-value override. It does not change Maximum, ability text or artwork, and the active alternate mode still governs whether positive Energy changes are allowed.

sections.title: After-Ultimate lock
paragraphs: Pause Energy after Ultimate blocks ordinary recovery until the next combat round after the standard cast. For example, a round-2 cast empties the orb and prevents normal awards for the rest of that round. Check both this lock and the active charge type when an orb seems stuck.
Enhanced standard Ultimates share the character’s existing Energy pool and regeneration settings. They do not create a second enhanced Energy reserve.

articles.title: Standard Ultimates: readiness, code and turn order
articles.summary: Keep charge, splash art, chat descriptions and optional code in one activation flow.

sections.title: Configure a standard Ultimate
paragraphs: Enable the Ultimate system, set Maximum Energy, then configure button/orb artwork, splash artwork, title/subtitle and Ultimate Text. Orb art appears in charge displays; splash art is the cast presentation; text is the chat description. These slots serve different purposes.

Optional Ultimate code is deliberate JavaScript in its code field. Descriptions are prose and do not need code to be displayed. Existing text-only kits still post their descriptions when activated. A returned string from code can supply text if the configured description is empty.

sections.title: Request and resolve
paragraphs: Floating orbs, the party HUD and supported hotbar/API requests use the same readiness and ownership checks. The active form supplies its charge system and ability configuration. A resolving lock prevents duplicate requests and conflicting progress edits.

An Ultimate outside its own turn can wait for another Main Party member’s normal turn before the module inserts its temporary turn. The actual cast runs its configured code, posts ability text and shows splash art. The Complete Ultimate flow removes the temporary entry and resumes the interrupted participant.

sections.title: Summoning reservations
paragraphs: A summoning Ultimate plans legal positions first. A queued cast revalidates its placement when its turn begins. If the scene changed, the player can reposition; a blocked or cancelled queued summon restores reserved charge and continues initiative. Merely reading the guide or previewing artwork never reserves charge.

articles.title: Alternate Ultimate orb builder
articles.summary: Design separate icon components and choose how the GM lights them.

sections.title: Replace the Energy orb
paragraphs: In HSR Settings, enable Alternate Ultimate. Its builder appears and the character uses its saved components in the floating orb, combat HUD and previews. Positive standard Energy gains are blocked while the active form uses alternate charge. Switching it off restores the regular Energy orb while retaining its saved alternate design and progress.
Alternate charge is assigned by GM controls. An image’s color, shape, file name or glow does not automatically award a counter for an attack or debuff.

sections.title: Build the artwork
steps: Open Ultimate Orb Builder and add a component, browse/upload images or drop supported artwork or Items.
Select a component from the layer list or canvas. Drag it to move, use handles to rotate/resize, or enter X/Y, Scale and Rotation numerically.
Choose the active image and optional off image. Without an off image, inactive art is greyed out from the active image.
Set the glow color or detect its main image color. Both per-component glow and overall active glow can be toggled.
Choose Free activation or Circular counter and configure its sequence when applicable.
Preview All off, All on or Live counters, then Save orb design. Preview switches do not change live charge.

sections.title: Readiness and layer order
paragraphs: Free activation exposes one GM checkbox per component; checking it lights that icon. Every component must be active before the Ultimate can be used. A successful cast resets alternate switches and circular progress.

Layers determine what is drawn on top. Sequence order determines circular charging; they are independent. Duplicate and reorder controls change the design, while Reset counters changes live progress. Normal and enhanced forms can keep different layouts and counters.

articles.imageAlt: Illustrated guide to Alternate Ultimate orb builder.
articles.imageCaption: Bundled illustration. Artwork, names and sample values can differ in your world; click to expand.

articles.title: Circular alternate counters and sequence order
articles.summary: A single counter lights a cumulative sequence from a chosen start.

sections.title: Configure the sequence
paragraphs: Choose Circular counter in the builder. Assign each component a unique Sequence order, select a Starting icon, and set the First activation number. The route follows sequence order from the chosen starting icon and wraps after the final order.

First activation number is the counter value at which the first icon lights. It does not change the number of components or their layer order. Each subsequent increment lights one more icon and keeps all previous icons lit.

sections.title: Worked four-icon example
paragraphs: With four components and First activation number 2, counter values 0 and 1 light nothing. Value 2 lights the starting icon, 3 lights two, 4 lights three and 5 lights all four. Decreasing the count extinguishes later icons for correction.

sections.title: Use and reset
paragraphs: The GM Panel and DM Combat show the numeric charge field and −/+ controls for the active form. They do not interpret attacks, skills or debuffs automatically. Edit orb changes the saved layout; Reset counters empties progress. Casting can happen only when every configured component is active and clears alternate charge afterward. Duplicate sequence numbers must be corrected before saving.

articles.title: Enhanced form and its independent Ultimate
articles.summary: Choose Standard or Alternate charge and copy or design enhanced artwork.

sections.title: Enable and switch
paragraphs: Enable Enhanced Stance in the sheet, then configure replacement Skill/Talent text, portraits, orb/splash artwork, token image and optional transition media. GM Panel and DM Combat → Stances switch the live form. Finish a resolving ability before changing it. Blank artwork overrides generally retain the normal counterpart.

Enhanced ability restrictions are mechanical configuration, while token transition media is a visual overlay during the change. The resulting token artwork comes from its separate enhanced token slot.

sections.title: Enhanced Ultimate type
paragraphs: Enable Enhance Ultimate, then use Enhanced Ultimate type: OFF means Standard and ON means Alternate. Standard shows the ordinary Energy orb, shared Current/Maximum Energy, regeneration and enhanced orb artwork. Alternate shows its custom components and builder tools. Enhanced text, code and splash art apply to either type.

Use regular alternate configuration copies the regular alternate orb’s saved layout, images, off images, glow, mode, sequence and starting settings. It is a copy, so later edits can differ. Design different layout opens the independent enhanced builder.

sections.title: Independent progress
paragraphs: The active form controls readiness, which orb is shown, which alternate counters are consumed and whether normal Energy gains are blocked. Regular and enhanced alternate counters remain independent; switching forms restores that form’s progress. Copying a layout preserves existing progress, and switching the type retains saved designs. Enhanced Standard uses the character’s existing Energy pool rather than a second one.

articles.title: Skills and shared Skill Point costs
articles.summary: Configure per-character Skill text, SP cost and optional HP or summon requirements.

sections.title: The per-character Skill
paragraphs: Enable Skill button makes the Skill available through its normal widgets. Skill Text is the description posted after a successful cast; Skill button artwork is the action’s circular image. The enhanced form can replace its text and artwork while using the same configured mechanical cost and summon workflow.
Skill descriptions are not executable JavaScript. Apply attacks, damage and custom effects through supported items, chat controls or explicitly implemented mechanics.

sections.title: Skill point cost
paragraphs: Choose 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or Custom. Zero is free; Custom reveals a whole-number cost field. The shared SP balance is party-wide, while this amount belongs to the character’s Skill. A cost of 2 with a balance of 5 leaves 3 after a successful cast.

Affordability is checked before the action commits. Successful casts deduct automatically; cancelled or impossible summons do not pay SP or HP. Editing the configured cost does not immediately spend SP. Use shared-resource controls to adjust the current party balance.

sections.title: Combine requirements
paragraphs: Has HP requirement adds its actual-HP cost in addition to SP. Summons creature adds an Actor choice and placement flow. A player needs normal Actor ownership and a connected GM for the authoritative action. A resolving lock prevents overlapping duplicate casts.

articles.title: HP requirements and dice costs
articles.summary: Round down percentage costs and pay actual HP only when a Skill commits.

sections.title: Choose the cost type
paragraphs: Enable Has HP requirement on the Skill. Half HP pays 50% of the selected basis, rounded down; 10% HP pays one tenth, rounded down. Percentage of selects Current HP (default) or Maximum HP. Custom constant is a fixed whole amount. Custom roll accepts strict xDy such as 2d6.

Dice are rolled once by the authority for that cast. x is the number of dice and y is the die size. Supported limits are 1–100 dice and 1–1000 sides. Additions, arbitrary expressions and JavaScript are not accepted in this cost field.

sections.title: Worked examples
paragraphs: At 39 current / 55 maximum HP, half-current costs floor(39/2) = 19. Half-maximum costs floor(55/2) = 27. Ten-percent-current costs 3, while ten-percent-maximum costs 5. A flat cost of 7 pays exactly 7. A 2d6 cost pays that one rolled total.

The character must have enough actual current HP to pay, regardless of the chosen maximum-HP basis. Temporary HP does not pay this requirement. Paying an exact balance can reduce actual HP to zero. It is a cost, not a normal incoming damage roll.

sections.title: Cancellation and commitment
paragraphs: HP is combined with the normal SP requirement. Illegal or cancelled summon placement spends neither. An HP cost preview or configuration edit does not itself deduct HP; the live ability cast performs the authority checks and payment. Repeated requests while resolving do not provide extra independent cost rolls.

articles.title: Shared SP, Technique Points and Punchline
articles.summary: Distinguish party balances, individual ability costs and combat resources.

sections.title: Shared Skill Points
paragraphs: The party uses one live Skill Point balance and a configured maximum. Character Skills choose their own costs from that pool. GM Panel and DM Combat −/+ controls change the live balance; Skill Point Configuration changes its presentation and limits. Refill is an explicit live refill, not a preview.
A character’s configured Skill cost does not change the pool until a successful cast. Light Cone effects can affect capacity or awards through their supported event rules.

sections.title: Technique Points and Talent Points
paragraphs: Technique Points are a separate shared out-of-combat ability resource. Talent Points belong to individual eligible combat characters and have their own maximum and overcap settings. These are not interchangeable pools merely because their widgets look similar.

sections.title: Punchline
paragraphs: Punchline is the shared Elation resource. Aha Configuration selects the Elation master switch and Path. Matching characters use their configured Punchline gain; other eligible damage events use their normal gain rule.

Override Punchline lets its meter display independently of the normal Elation master-switch visibility. DM Combat → Show Punchline restores the display. Override does not freeze the total or force an Aha critical hit. Meter icon, number font and offsets affect presentation, not the amount.

articles.title: Skill and Ultimate creature summoning
articles.summary: Link existing Actors and place full-size animated tokens inside a valid zone.

sections.title: Build the summon list
paragraphs: Enable Summons creature in the Skill or Ultimate settings. Drag existing world Actors from the directory into its list, or choose Add existing Actor. Drag rows to reorder choices. Count is the number of copies of the selected creature to place. Skill and Ultimate lists and radii are independent, and enhanced abilities use their character’s configured mechanical lists.
Source Actors are references, not copied Actor definitions. Placed tokens inherit the source Actor’s prototype size and settings. Linking the source does not rename or change its base Actor.

sections.title: Range, footprint and barriers
paragraphs: Summoning radius uses the scene’s distance units: 30 ft means six 5-ft squares of distance. The entire token footprint must be inside the valid radius and scene bounds, clear of other tokens and lighting-blocking walls. A creature cannot cross or straddle a lighting barrier even if movement is permitted. Open doors and relevant wall levels are respected.

The chooser marks a creature Cannot Fit when there is no valid footprint. If no choice fits, the cast is cancelled without costs. A GM validates ownership, saved choice, quantity, token dimensions, occupancy, range and barriers before creation.

sections.title: Place the creatures
steps: Use the Skill or charged Ultimate and choose an available configured creature.
Inspect highlighted valid anchor squares; hover a square to preview its full footprint.
Click one square for each requested copy. Undo removes a pending placement.
Cancel, Escape or right-click abandons placement without paying the normal Skill costs.
After a successful cast the tokens appear with a brief animation. Generic ability summons do not automatically receive initiative entries.

sections.title: Queued Ultimates and failure recovery
paragraphs: A queued Ultimate reserves charge and rechecks placement when its temporary turn begins. If its selected space is no longer valid, reposition. A cancelled or blocked queued summon restores the original Energy or alternate counters and continues initiative. Partial token-creation failures are cleaned up. Ending combat restores reserved summoning charges.
Blocked casts do not trigger successful-cast resource rewards. This is separate from the companion addon’s adjacent-square summon and automatic initiative behavior.

articles.title: Talents and Talent Points
articles.summary: Manage individual combat resources and read Talent descriptions.

sections.title: Talent text and eligibility
paragraphs: Talent Text describes the character’s Talent and can be viewed from its widget or the combat panel. Talent Points are individual, unlike the shared SP pool. An eligible character must be in an active combat and on its battlefield/initiative roster; outside that context its live pool is unavailable.

Current Talent Points reset for a new combat while its configured maximum is preserved. Maximum is the trigger threshold. Overcap Maximum limits how much may be held beyond that threshold. A zero threshold disables readiness-triggered Talent turns.

sections.title: Reaching the threshold
paragraphs: The GM can adjust current points through the supported resource fields and −/+ controls. Reaching a positive trigger threshold queues the module’s Talent turn flow. The active encounter and resolving-action rules determine insertion; repeatedly clicking is not a legitimate way to duplicate the temporary turn.
The point icon, scale and text presentation can be configured separately. Hiding the summoner’s Talent on a companion HUD affects its display and does not turn that character’s Talent into shared SP.

sections.title: Automation limits
paragraphs: Do not assume a Talent description or a legacy Talent script field is an active general event interpreter. The current event dispatcher forwards supported events to Light Cone automation; custom kit behavior needs an explicit supported workflow or deliberate code. Use live point controls when no automation implements the intended award.

articles.title: Techniques outside combat
articles.summary: Configure pre-combat descriptions, artwork and shared Technique Points.

sections.title: Configuration
paragraphs: Enable the character’s Technique and enter its description and button artwork. The description is posted by the successful Technique flow. The separate Technique Point configuration controls the shared amount, maximum, icon and display options.
Technique Points are distinct from the Talent pool, even when an abbreviation could be read as TP. Hover the field or use its full name to confirm which resource you are editing.

sections.title: Using a Technique
paragraphs: Use the normal owned-character action outside active initiative, with enough shared Technique Points and a connected GM when authority is required. The ordinary use consumes its Technique resource. Merely opening the description or configuring artwork does not use the ability.

If the button is disabled, check that it is enabled for that character, that combat is not already running and that the shared pool is available. Descriptive pre-battle benefits still need their explicit supported item or effect implementation.

articles.title: Turn flow, interrupts and completion buttons
articles.summary: Keep ordinary, Ultimate, Elation, Talent and Action Advance turns distinct.

sections.title: Ordinary and inserted turns
paragraphs: Ordinary initiative participants remain the encounter’s baseline. An off-turn Ultimate, an Elation action, a ready Talent or Action Advance can add a temporary turn with its own purpose. Main Party waiting rules affect when queued Ultimates begin. A temporary entry is not an additional permanent token or Actor.

Use the matching completion button after resolving an Ultimate or Elation Action. The module removes that temporary participant and resumes the appropriate interrupted turn. Next/Previous Turn affect the live initiative state and should be used deliberately.

sections.title: Queue and cleanup
paragraphs: Ultimate charge can be reserved while waiting. Summoning placement is validated again at the actual cast. If it is no longer legal, reposition or cancel; cancellation restores reserved charge and continues initiative. Ending combat cleans up its reserved and temporary state.

When the tracker appears stuck, inspect the current temporary participant and relevant completion chat card before deleting entries manually. Readiness, ownership and resolving locks prevent ordinary duplicate activation.

articles.title: The full Star Rail GM Panel
articles.summary: Live resources, character tuning, temporary weaknesses and editor launchers.

sections.title: Live party resources
paragraphs: Punchline and Shared Skill Points are current party-wide balances. Their number fields set a total immediately; −/+ adjusts by the indicated step. Override Punchline changes meter availability independently of the usual master-switch visibility. It does not make Aha crit or prevent future resource changes.

Place Character Action Button selects an Actor and Skill/Ultimate action, then creates the GM’s movable action widget. It does not cast immediately. Blow Up Tatsuo opens or places its separate configured visual effect.

sections.title: Encounter and interface controls
paragraphs: Special Action Advance inserts one extra turn for an existing initiative participant. Boss Phase Controls opens live multi-phase boss controls. Carousel configuration enables the tracker, permits resizing and sets its maximum width and visible length. Show scene navigator and nameplate affects that display.
The carousel preview demonstrates presentation; Save Carousel commits configuration. Moving or resizing it affects UI layout rather than token positions or initiative scores.

sections.title: Temporary weaknesses
paragraphs: NPC rows show permanent sheet weaknesses and temporary selections. Permanent ones cannot be unchecked as temporary entries. Save Temporary Weaknesses applies the selection; Reset returns to sheet-defined weaknesses. All/None overrides temporary Toughness matching rather than changing the NPC’s base damage resistances.
Bulk actions affect scene enemies covered by the panel. Reset Scene Toughness restores configured Toughness maxima; Reset weaknesses restores the weakness configuration. These are different actions.

sections.title: Character Resources and launchers
paragraphs: Per-character fields edit Energy, Maximum, REGEN score, attack/hit awards, Punchline gain, Talent current/maximum and the after-Ultimate lock. Main Party, GM Party Override and Receives Rewards control separate rules. Enhanced Stance and alternate counters refer to that character’s active form.

Rows collapse without changing values. Module Configuration opens specialized Aha, SP, Element, Path, Recipe and Eidolon tools. A launcher opens an editor; it does not automatically save a draft or spend an activation currency.

articles.title: DM Combat: every tab and footer control
articles.summary: Use encounter-focused tabs and always-available resource and turn controls.

sections.title: Encounter tabs

rows: Active-form free component switches or circular counter; Reset empties charge and Edit opens the design.
View descriptions and adjust eligible combat Talent Points.
Lock/unlock temporary controls; toggle Elements or choose All, None or Reset.
Switch configured characters between Normal and Enhanced.
Open the recurring damage, condition and Light Cone editor.
Select among configured phases for live multi-phase bosses.

sections.note: Disabled actions may require an active encounter, an eligible combatant or a configured feature. A lock is not removed by hovering help.

sections.title: Footer actions
paragraphs: View Adjusted PC Stats opens effective combat values and automatic baselines. Show Punchline restores its meter. Punchline and Skill Points −/+ change live shared balances. Previous and Next move initiative. Action Advance selects an existing participant for one extra turn. End Combat finishes the encounter.

Footer controls are live actions, except windows opened solely for inspection. A phase change, stance switch, resource edit or turn advance can immediately affect play. Use each tooltip to distinguish current state from a preview.

sections.title: Avoid confusing controls
paragraphs: Lock Weaknesses protects that NPC’s temporary controls; it does not change its permanent sheet weaknesses. Edit orb opens a draft designer; component checkboxes change live readiness. View Talent reads text; its neighboring −/+ changes points. An unavailable Planar combat-stats integration must be installed/updated before its editor can work.
