articles.title: NPC Toughness and Element weaknesses
articles.summary: Separate base weaknesses, temporary overrides and current Toughness.

sections.title: Configure the NPC
paragraphs: Enable Toughness and choose its maximum and permanent Element weaknesses on the NPC configuration. Current Toughness tracks the live breakable bar. Matching attacks can reduce it according to the module’s normal damage rules. The weakness icons can also display discovered weakness information.

A permanent weakness is a sheet setting. Temporary GM weakness selections and All/None modes are encounter controls. Discovered display history is another separate value. Resetting one does not necessarily reset the others.

sections.title: Temporary changes and locks
paragraphs: The GM Panel and DM Combat Weaknesses tab expose temporary Elements, Reset and All/None modes. Lock controls prevent incidental changes in the combat panel. Permanent sheet-selected Elements remain protected in temporary checklists.

Reset Scene Toughness restores each Toughness-enabled scene NPC to its own configured maximum, preserving maximums and weakness definitions. Reset Discovered Weaknesses clears discovery display history. Neither action is a normal HP heal.

sections.title: What matching means
paragraphs: Element IDs must agree between character and target. A display name or icon alone is not a new damage-resistance rule. Temporary Toughness weakness does not automatically rewrite D&D5e resistance, immunity or vulnerability fields. Use the supported damage application to keep Toughness and HP processing together.

articles.title: Break and Super Break characters
articles.summary: Read the added BREAK score and the module’s actual damage formulas.

sections.title: Break Effect
paragraphs: The Break Effect score uses floor((score − 10)/2), with the configured score limited to 1–30. The sheet’s added BREAK card edits this same value. Weakness Break uses the configured dice count and die size when the character reduces Toughness to zero.

Normal Break damage is floor(dice total × max(1, Break Effect modifier)). The minimum multiplier of 1 prevents a nonpositive modifier from making that break roll vanish. Example: 2d6 totals 7 and modifier +3 produces 21.

sections.title: Break Character and Super Break
paragraphs: A Break Character’s successful ordinary attack deals 1 HP damage and directs its full rolled damage to Toughness. Ordinary non-Break attacks use their damage dice for Toughness rather than treating every flat bonus as dice damage.

Can deal Super Break enables eligible hits against an already broken enemy to roll the configured Break dice plus (Break Effect modifier + 1). Example: dice total 7 and modifier +3 produces 11 Super Break damage. This is not the same multiplication used by Weakness Break.

sections.title: Apply the damage
paragraphs: Break/Super Break rolls post their supported damage cards. Use Apply Damage to carry out the HP application; displaying a roll is not proof that HP has already changed. Their typography and Element colors are configured in Damage/Break appearance, separate from these formulas.

articles.title: Chat damage controls and application tracking
articles.summary: Use the module’s supported roll and Apply Damage flow.

sections.title: Roll and target
paragraphs: The module tracks relevant damage roll cards and their source, targets and kind. Apply Damage uses the actual supported application workflow, including HP, Toughness and Break behavior. A displayed number or descriptive ability paragraph is not an automatic HP change.

Confirm the intended target and damage type before applying. A non-Break hit, a Break Character hit and a Break/Super Break roll have different processing. The card’s recorded applications help identify what has already been applied.

sections.title: Avoid duplicate application
paragraphs: Use one authoritative damage application path for a given result. If another automation has already applied damage, inspect the card and target HP before applying it again manually. The module records application identity and results to guard its own duplicate processing.

Critical thresholds and damage bonuses can come from equipment and compatible Planar integration. Read Adjusted PC Stats for effective values; do not assume a visually larger number means the target has been changed.

articles.title: Aha Instant, Punchline and Elation Actions
articles.summary: Configure the final initiative participant and its following action sequence.

sections.title: Enable the system
paragraphs: Aha Configuration’s Elation master switch and selected Elation Path govern the normal Aha/Punchline features. Add Aha Instant to initiative creates the special participant when initiative is rolled. Add/Refresh Aha Combatant Now updates it in the current encounter.

Aha is placed one point below the lowest ordinary initiative score, so it follows the existing participants. The initiative preview’s sample numeral is presentation, not a promise that its live initiative is always zero.

sections.title: Resolve the sequence
paragraphs: At Aha’s turn, matching living Elation characters receive temporary Elation Action turns immediately afterward in their existing initiative order. Each posts its configured action description. Its owner uses Complete Elation Action after resolving it.

After the final action, the temporary sequence is removed, Punchline resets and normal combat resumes. Aha’s video, floating button and Punchline icon/font controls affect presentation. Preview Locally shows media on the current client and does not run the complete encounter sequence.

sections.title: Critical turns
paragraphs: The Joyseeker Light Cone can enable Aha critical behavior for a turn. Its separate GM question confirms whether another source already enabled that critical. It is not the same as Override Punchline, the Aha artwork preview or the initiative refresh action.

articles.title: As the Joyseeker Remembers It: Aha critical check
articles.summary: Understand the automatic d20 check and the GM’s other-source question.

sections.title: Eligibility and roll
paragraphs: The Light Cone must be eligible through its equipment/attunement workflow. Its critical threshold benefit depends on Elation allies with distinct Elements. When Aha Instant occurs, the automated d20 is compared with the wearer’s effective critical threshold; meeting or exceeding it succeeds.
On success, Aha can crit that turn and Elation Action damage uses the corresponding doubled behavior. This is turn state, not a permanent replacement for every character’s weapon critical range.

sections.title: The GM popup
paragraphs: The GM is asked whether at least one other player/source already enabled Aha to crit. Answer Yes only if another source supplied that ability. Yes grants 5 base Energy to Elation characters before their regeneration bonuses and posts the Light Cone information. No posts its information with “AHA INSTANT CAN NOW CRIT”.

The question supplements the automatic wearer roll; it is not a request to manually roll that same d20. An eligible active GM, correct equipped item, Aha event and successful threshold check are prerequisites. Alternate Ultimate Energy-gain restrictions still apply to those characters.

sections.title: If it did not appear
paragraphs: Check equipment eligibility, selected Elation Path and Elements, effective threshold, the roll result, active GM and current module version. A failed check does not produce the successful critical branch. See the encounter chat and DoT/Light Cone runtime controls before manually awarding an additional copy of Energy.

articles.title: Multi-phase bosses
articles.summary: Configure replacement Actors, inherited bar layout and live phase changes.

sections.title: Configure the chain
paragraphs: Is Boss enables the shared boss HP display while the Actor is in active combat. Phase count selects the number of represented phases. Drag replacement Actors into Phase 2/3 slots; their tokens replace the current phase when its HP reaches zero.

Phase token dimensions are grid units. A zero dimension inherits that phase Actor’s prototype-token size. Each phase Actor supplies its own portrait and crop. Phase 1’s bar layout controls the encounter-wide presentation.

sections.title: Control and inspect
paragraphs: Show Phase Controls opens the live phase window, and DM Combat → Phases offers the configured choices. Changing a phase is a real token/encounter operation, not an artwork preview. Review source Actors and token space before using it.
Boss bar width and HP/Toughness heights are display pixels. Portrait X/Y and scale adjust its crop. These values do not change the creature’s HP maximum or battle-map size.

articles.title: HSR initiative carousel and Action Advance
articles.summary: Arrange the tracker and insert a deliberate extra turn.

sections.title: Carousel presentation
paragraphs: The HSR tracker stays at the left edge. Its top-left grip changes vertical position and its resize handle changes width/visible length within configured limits. Enable/Allow resizing and maximum dimensions are GM interface settings, not initiative bonuses.

Reusable frame colors supply default identity treatments. A per-character override can force its chosen frame/dot color. Initiative portrait artwork has its own crop and enhanced-form replacement; it is separate from the HUD portrait and Actor token image.

sections.title: Action Advance
paragraphs: Choose an existing initiative participant in the GM Panel or DM Combat Action Advance picker. Confirming inserts one extra turn and then returns to the interrupted participant. The picker can include Aha Instant. It does not create a new world Actor or grant permanent initiative duplicates.
Previous/Next controls advance live combat. If an inserted Ultimate or Elation Action is current, use its matching completion flow. Reading an initiative preview does not progress the round.

articles.title: Light Cone equipment and eligibility
articles.summary: Effects depend on equipped, eligible items and supported event rules.

sections.title: Install the item
paragraphs: The module supplies a Light Cone loot type, frame presentation and compendium content. Import a cone onto the intended Actor and equip/attune it through the designated Light Cone slot workflow. Merely owning a named Item or viewing its artwork is not enough to activate its effects.

Eligibility can depend on Path and the supported item definition. Use the item’s actual effect description and the compatible automation rules rather than assuming an arbitrary renamed Item will implement a full kit.

sections.title: Runtime effects
paragraphs: Supported Light Cones can change stats, stacks, cooldowns, resource awards, DoT or event-triggered effects. The DoT/Light Cone editor exposes live counters and ability classification. Cooldown counters may record the Actor turn at which an effect last triggered, rather than a number of turns remaining.

Damage and resource events are GM-authoritative and guarded against duplicate/recursive processing. Adjusted PC Stats shows compatible effective combat values. Unequipping or losing eligibility removes the item from the normal eligible-effect path.

sections.title: Known special cases
paragraphs: Joyseeker uses the Aha critical flow described separately. Sleep Like the Dead’s noncritical/no-damage trigger uses the translated threshold benefit in this module, rather than assuming the original video-game percentage. Do not manually apply a second copy of an effect already handled by its supported rule.

articles.title: Damage over time and tracked conditions
articles.summary: Assign recurring damage and manage its remaining ticks.

sections.title: Apply a DoT
paragraphs: Start combat and open DM Combat → DoT → Open DoT & Light Cone editor. Select Target, optional Source, DoT type, damage attribute, dice count/size and turn count, then Apply DoT. Source identifies whose eligible modifiers apply; No source uses base damage.

DoT type identifies the condition for cone rules, while damage attribute controls resistance/immunity processing. Burn/shock/bleed/wind shear identity is therefore separate from the damage attribute selection. Damage is rolled and applied at the affected creature’s turn start.

sections.title: Duration and editing
paragraphs: Turn count defines remaining future ticks. Effects clear after their final tick. Current effect rows show their base dice, attribute and ticks left; editing remaining duration or Remove changes the live effect. Source die upgrades are applied when the tick rolls.

Tracked conditions use the selected target and duration with a condition classification and penalty magnitude. Assigning a condition is not the same action as rolling DoT damage. Check reduced AC, slowed, implanted weakness or other-debuff classification for the intended rule.

sections.title: Light Cone controls
paragraphs: Actor sections show their eligible cone, stored stacks/cooldowns, DoTs and conditions. Ability classifications help supported cone rules distinguish attack types; a prose name alone is not a guaranteed classification. Runtime counters are mechanical data, separate from the visual remaining-ticks label.

articles.title: Adjusted PC combat stats and temporary buffs
articles.summary: Compare effective values with their automatic baselines.

sections.title: Inspect before editing
paragraphs: View Adjusted PC Stats requires the compatible Planar combat-buff integration and an active combat. It shows effective encounter values and the automatic baseline. Manual adjustments are tracked separately from permanent sheet data.

AC, HP and speed bonuses are additive to their original values through the supported integration. Speed bonuses should add distance, rather than replace the character’s base walking speed. Show Original/automatic baseline helps distinguish the sheet value from encounter changes.

sections.title: Critical values
paragraphs: Critical Rate reduces the effective d20 critical threshold: for example a +3 rate benefit against a base threshold of 20 gives 17. The effective threshold combines the applicable sheet/equipment/integration values. Critical Damage Bonus is a separate additive damage benefit.

Reset buffs for one character clears its manual encounter adjustments rather than editing its permanent ability scores. A disabled or unavailable editor can indicate an outdated/missing Planar integration, not that the Actor’s ordinary stats were deleted.

articles.title: Memosprite setup and linked sources
articles.summary: Configure the companion addon’s source, HP, resource and ability list.

sections.title: Separate addon, integrated help
paragraphs: Tely’s Memosprites supplies the companion character tab and HUD behavior. Ultimates supplies this documentation and contextual hover help when that addon is installed. Enabling Help does not install the companion addon or change the Path rules in an older installed version.
A GM configures the companion; owners retain permitted summon/ability actions. Open its character Memosprite tab or configuration link. The companion’s saved settings belong to the summoner Actor.

sections.title: Source and identity
paragraphs: Drag an Actor or Item into the source slot to link its UUID and display information. Memosprite name is a separate display label and does not rename the summoner. A valid world Actor is needed for the placed-creature workflow; an Item supplies a reference/art but is not itself a creature Actor.

An Actor source supplies live HP from its sheet, so Current HP and Maximum HP in the configuration become disabled. Edit HP on that linked Actor. Without linked Actor HP, the addon uses its manual values.

sections.title: Setup order
steps: Enable Has a memosprite and link the intended source.
Choose its name, tab icon and circular HUD portrait.
Set its resource type and current/maximum values, then add up to five abilities.
Choose visible HUD parts and arrange them in the designer.
Place the summoner on the map and test the actual summon action with its owner and GM.

articles.imageAlt: Illustrated guide to Memosprite setup and linked sources.
articles.imageCaption: Bundled illustration. Artwork, names and sample values can differ in your world; click to expand.

articles.title: Memosprite HUD and portrait designer
articles.summary: Move the whole frame or individual visible parts independently.

sections.title: Visibility
paragraphs: Show HUD name controls the bottom character name. Hide summoner Talent affects the summoner’s Talent widget while the companion is enabled. Show floating Summon button controls that local companion launcher. Portrait, HP arc, HP number, resource and abilities each have their own visibility setting.

The unsummoned portrait is normally greyed out; summoned state reveals the live HP and selected additions according to the configured visibility. Preview summoned changes the designer’s sample state, not the battle-map creature.

sections.title: Frame versus parts
paragraphs: Frame X/Y and width position the complete companion HUD. Whole HUD scale changes the complete design. Portrait, HP text, resource and abilities each have their own X/Y offsets and scale. Drag a part in the preview to place it, scroll to scale, or enter its numeric values. Dragging empty frame space moves the group.

Offsets are pixels in this editor, while scale is percent of base size. These controls do not move a map token, change its footprint or grant combat bonuses. Restore/Remove from HUD changes part visibility rather than deleting its underlying ability.

sections.title: Portrait crop
paragraphs: Open portrait editor controls the circular image, crop X/Y and crop scale. Drag inside its circle to reposition and scroll to zoom, or enter the values. Save Portrait applies that editor; Cancel leaves its pending crop unconfirmed. The tab icon and source Actor token artwork are separate image slots.

articles.imageAlt: Illustrated guide to Memosprite HUD and portrait designer.
articles.imageCaption: Bundled illustration. Artwork, names and sample values can differ in your world; click to expand.

articles.title: Memosprite resources and abilities
articles.summary: Use a counter, up-to-three dots or a percentage with a five-ability kit.

sections.title: Resource styles
paragraphs: X/Y counter displays current against maximum. Usage dots display up to three charges. Fang percentage uses a percent display with a 100 maximum. The numeric counter supports a larger configured maximum. Resource style changes the companion’s display/limits, not the party SP pool.

Current resource is the spendable live amount. Maximum is its cap. Restore resource explicitly refills it. Inactive dots are simply the companion’s unfilled charges; their appearance can differ between installed addon versions.

sections.title: Abilities
paragraphs: Add up to five abilities. Name is the button label; Description is its explanatory chat text; optional Damage formula is its supported damage roll; Resource cost spends the companion resource; Icon supplies that button’s art. Use runs the ability and checks its available companion resource.

Remove ability deletes that entry from the companion kit, not the linked source Actor. These costs are separate from the summoner’s shared Skill Points and the base module’s Skill HP requirement. Configuration saves through the addon’s normal automatic flow.

articles.title: Summoning and unsummoning a Memosprite
articles.summary: Place the linked companion adjacent to its summoner and track its token.

sections.title: Prepare and place
paragraphs: Use a valid linked world Actor and put the summoner’s owned token on the current scene. The addon’s summon action highlights available surrounding squares. The player or GM chooses a valid position; the linked Actor’s token appears there, its HUD portrait becomes active and the addon adds the companion to initiative.

This is the companion addon’s adjacent-square workflow. The base module’s Skill/Ultimate summon list instead has a configurable range, count and lighting-barrier validation and does not automatically create initiative entries.

sections.title: Unsummon and recover
paragraphs: Unsummon removes the addon’s tracked companion token/combat participant and returns its HUD to the inactive state. A configuration source drop links data; it does not itself perform a summon. Show floating summon button now displays the launcher without placing a creature.

If the action is unavailable, check Has a memosprite, owner permissions, a valid Actor source, summoner token, scene space and installed addon version/Path rules. Do not confuse a designer’s summoned preview with an actual map token.

articles.title: Artwork, image paths and coordinate systems
articles.summary: Choose the right image slot and distinguish pixels, percentages and token units.

sections.title: Image slots have different jobs
paragraphs: Actor portrait is the general fallback image. Combat HUD portrait is the party lineup artwork. Initiative portrait belongs to the tracker. Orb/button art sits inside an action/charge display. Splash art is the cast presentation. Messenger portrait is the circular chat identity. Enhanced and boss forms can supply their own replacements.

Use each slot’s file picker or supported image drop target. The same file can be reused, but changing one slot does not automatically rewrite every other portrait. A Foundry-accessible path must load for all clients; a private local drive path is not a shared asset.

sections.title: Units and crop
paragraphs: X/Y can mean a percentage center in one editor and pixels of offset in another. Scale is a display percentage: 100% is base size. Token width/height use grid units. Summon radius uses the scene’s distance units. Read the field tooltip rather than transferring a number between unrelated editors.

Flip mirrors the rendered image without editing the source file. Hue, saturation and brightness affect a visual overlay. A crop or font does not change attack range, token footprint or mechanical statistics.

sections.title: Readable assets
paragraphs: Transparent PNG/WebP/SVG images preserve a silhouette where supported. Keep icons legible at their actual small HUD size. Test the cast splash at the clients’ screen sizes and use Preload when large images create delays. Expand manual screenshots to inspect their sample labels.

articles.title: Combat Party HUD designer
articles.summary: Arrange portraits, action orbs and companion overlays.

sections.title: Layout and preview
paragraphs: The combat Party HUD groups character portraits, HP and configured action indicators. Its designer adjusts the saved display arrangement; previews show artwork and relative positions without casting abilities. Drag the relevant grip or element, resize within its control limits and save the design.

Character portrait crop settings determine how its art fits the frame. The active form supplies enhanced replacements where configured. Alternate Ultimate components replace the normal Energy orb artwork in their active charge mode.

sections.title: Ready and consumed state
paragraphs: The Ultimate ready glow is above the portrait and behind the orb, inset under its edge. It disappears when the charge is consumed. A grey component indicates alternate charge state rather than a missing Actor image.

An enabled companion addon can overlay its own memosprite design onto the summoner’s HUD card, subject to its visibility settings. Local widget placement and per-character portrait configuration are different saved values.

articles.title: Ultimate splash art, title cards and preloading
articles.summary: Configure the cast image and title separately from the charging orb.

sections.title: Splash layout
paragraphs: Ultimate splash art is shown by the cast presentation. X/Y, scale, title placement, title size, alignment, subtitle and fonts control its composition. These are distinct from the Ultimate orb image and the character’s ordinary combat portrait.

Enhanced Ultimate artwork can replace the standard splash when that enhanced ability is active. Missing enhanced art can use the normal counterpart where the configuration supports fallback. Test actual active-form casts after arranging the preview.

sections.title: Loading and timing
paragraphs: Preload Splash Art fetches/decodes the configured images on clients before a cast needs them. It does not grant charge, run Ultimate code or insert an extra turn. Large media can still take time to transfer; verify that all clients can access the image path.

Previewing a splash is a local presentation test. A real Ultimate request performs the separate ownership, readiness, charge, chat/code and combat flow. If a cast works but art is missing, check the active form’s image slot and asset load before changing mechanical charge.

articles.title: Enhanced token artwork and transition overlays
articles.summary: Keep the resulting token image separate from its switching animation.

sections.title: Result versus overlay
paragraphs: Enhanced token image is the artwork the token should use while the form is active. Transition media plays visually during the stance switch. Set normal/enhanced art and the overlay in their respective slots so the temporary animation does not become the permanent token image.

Position, scale, duration, flip, hue, saturation and brightness tune the overlay. They are presentation settings; they do not resize the token’s mechanical footprint or modify HP. Use a suitable transparent image/animation and a Foundry-accessible path.

sections.title: Preview and test
paragraphs: Use the transition preview to arrange the visual, then test an actual stance switch with a token on the scene. The GM Panel and DM Combat use the saved enhanced state. The normal art should return when the stance is turned off.

When the picture seems wrong, check the actual token art slot, active form and saved transition configuration independently. The enhanced Skill/Ultimate art and initiative portrait are additional, separate replacements.

articles.title: Damage, Break and Super Break appearance
articles.summary: Configure shared typography and Element-driven color treatments.

sections.title: Three visual categories
paragraphs: Damage, Break and Super Break have separate font files, sizes, bold choices, gradient switches and colors. Inherit Element color uses the relevant Element treatment instead of forcing the custom color pair. Top and bottom colors define the gradient when enabled.

Font files can be selected/uploaded through Foundry storage. Supported webfont formats should be accessible to connected clients. Size is display pixels at the configured baseline, not extra damage or a token scale.

sections.title: Preview versus mechanics
paragraphs: The preview shows text appearance and sample values. Save applies the shared styling. Ordinary damage, Break and Super Break calculations remain determined by their own mechanical rules and damage cards.

A critical-hit label is presentation of the recorded damage state; changing its color does not change the effective critical threshold. Use Adjusted PC Stats and item effects for supported critical mechanics.

articles.title: HSR phone hub and button designer
articles.summary: Customize per-character phones and their live menu destinations.

sections.title: Live hub versus designer
paragraphs: HSR Hub is the actual launcher. The GM can view a character’s phone and open Configure Phone for that profile. The designer preview shows that profile’s wallpaper, pose and buttons. Clicking or dragging a preview button edits its layout rather than triggering the live menu destination.

Player character selects the edited profile. Pose image/X/Y/zoom/flip controls the character illustration. Wallpaper fit, X/Y and zoom control the screen background. The per-character wallpaper library can save an image for an individual PC and open that phone for further editing.

sections.title: Buttons and snapping
paragraphs: Add a Button creates a layout entry with label, icon class, Opens destination, optional sheet tab/CSS target, width/height and position. Drag it in the preview; use its resize handle or dimensions. Double width expands that button’s footprint in the phone layout.

Snap to grid and Grid size affect positioning in the designer. They are UI percentages/grid steps, not battle-map squares or spell range. Removing a phone button does not remove the destination feature or underlying Actor.

sections.title: Player standard
paragraphs: Save as Player Standard stores the current layout as a reusable template. Load Standard copies that saved template into the current editing workflow. Apply Standard to All PCs applies it across player profiles. These operations can replace configured layouts; review the preview and profile before committing.
Phone actions keep their normal permissions. A player-visible layout does not grant access to GM-only configuration, and an optional addon’s button requires that addon to be enabled.

articles.title: HSR Messenger and contacts
articles.summary: Manage conversations, speakers, unread state and GM contact availability.

sections.title: Contacts and conversations
paragraphs: Contacts shows characters available for new conversations. The GM’s Configure Contacts enables which characters appear to players; this restriction does not apply to the GM. Jump to a character scrolls to its availability row, while Filter contacts narrows the visible list. Save Contact Availability commits the checkboxes.

Messages lists existing text chains and unread indicators. Select a chain to read it. Make Group Chat selects its members and group title; its search filters choices without sending a message. Player owners of selected characters can read and reply through the normal rules.

sections.title: Writing as a character
paragraphs: The GM’s Speaking as dropdown chooses the message’s speaker Actor. Write text, then press Send to publish to that thread. Selecting a speaker does not rename the logged-in user or alter the Actor’s sheet. Messenger portrait and crop settings determine the character’s chat identity image.

PC only filters the GM’s thread view. Deleting a message or text chain changes its saved conversation content, unlike simply clearing a search. Hover help and the manual never send messages or reveal a hidden conversation.

sections.title: Unread and drafts
paragraphs: Unread counts/dots identify unseen messages; they are not combat debuffs. A different selected thread has its own content and speaker context. Confirm the selected chain and speaker before sending. The ordinary interface retains its configured behavior on updates; documentation only explains the controls.

articles.title: Mission Manager, stages and objectives
articles.summary: Prepare hidden missions, assign recipients and track progress separately from rewards.

sections.title: Prepare and activate
paragraphs: Mission Manager is the GM browser with search and status filters. New Mission prepares an entry privately. Edit its title, type, location, optional card image and description. Assignment checkboxes select Main Party or other player characters. Activate for Players makes it visible; Hide from Players reverses that visibility.

Mission type supplies default icon/background, while a mission-specific card image overrides that background for this entry. A filter or collapsed list changes only the browser view, not saved mission visibility.

sections.title: Stages and objectives
paragraphs: Current Stage selects the active stage. Stage title names it; Add Stage creates another stage; Add Objective creates an entry within the selected stage. Each objective has text, Hidden, Revealed and Done fields. Hidden/Reveal affects its player-facing content, while Done records completion.

Save Mission commits the editor. Mark Complete records mission completion. Distribute Rewards is a separate live inventory grant; completing an objective or mission does not mean its Item rewards have already been distributed.

sections.title: Player log and archive
paragraphs: The Mission Log shows accessible missions and their stages/revealed objectives. Hidden and archived states are distinct from active/complete progress. Use the normal reward and archive workflow to preserve which missions have been rewarded. Deleting a prepared mission is a saved-content operation, not merely closing its card.

articles.title: Mission rewards and distribution
articles.summary: Know who receives Items and how Split differs from Copy mode.

sections.title: Configure the reward
paragraphs: Drag Item documents into the mission’s reward area. Each entry keeps its Item reference, quantity, artwork and rarity. Quantity is a whole count, while rarity changes its presentation and sorting rather than multiplying it. Remove Reward deletes that mission’s reference, not the source Item or previously granted inventory copies.

Assignments and eligibility determine recipients. Characters with non-GM owners and GM-controlled characters marked Receives Rewards can qualify. Main Party membership is not itself a substitute for assignment.

sections.title: Split or copy
paragraphs: Split total evenly divides the listed quantity among eligible assigned characters. Each gets the whole-number share and any remainder goes to randomly selected recipients. Full copy per assigned character grants the full listed amount to each eligible recipient.

sections.title: Live distribution and repeat prevention
paragraphs: Distribute Rewards grants the inventory Items and records claimed/distributed state. The normal workflow prevents repeated grants through the same completed reward state. Completion and distribution are separate; inspect both when a player reports missing loot.

Before a live grant, verify assignments, Receives Rewards, Item UUID, quantities and mode. Reading the reward icon or hovering Quantity does not grant an Item. Recreating the Item manually and then distributing again can duplicate the intended reward.

articles.title: Mission types, rarity hierarchy and backgrounds
articles.summary: Configure reusable mission and reward presentation.

sections.title: Types
paragraphs: Mission Settings defines mission type name, enabled state, order, icon and background. Enabled types appear in the supported mission views. Order sorts entries; it is not character level, difficulty or reward quantity. The All Missions icon has its own field.
A mission can override its type background with a mission-specific card image. Removing a type should be considered alongside existing mission assignments so stable references remain understandable.

sections.title: Rarities
paragraphs: Rarity entries define name, order, color and background for reward treatment. Their hierarchy controls visual organization rather than creating hidden damage bonuses or multiplying the Item count. Use accessible image paths and test contrast with the reward artwork.
Add/Remove controls change the catalog draft and Save commits its supported configuration. A type or rarity file picker selects artwork; it does not create a mission or distribute rewards.

articles.title: Party crafting, reagents and recipe cards
articles.summary: Learn a recipe and exchange configured ingredients for its output.

sections.title: Discover recipes
paragraphs: The crafting browser groups available recipes and supports filtering. A recipe must be available under its party/unlock rules. Recipe unlock cards are Items created by the recipe editor; redeeming a card teaches its corresponding recipe through the normal workflow. Owning an arbitrary similarly named Item is not automatically an unlock.

The source recipe defines its ingredients and crafted result. Quantity controls affect how many crafts are requested and therefore how many ingredients are needed. Inspect the selected Actor/party inventory context before committing.

sections.title: Craft deliberately
paragraphs: The live craft validates available ingredients, removes the required amounts and creates the defined output. A card preview or recipe selection does not consume materials. An ingredient count and an output count have different meanings, even if they display the same number.

Redeem All handles supported recipe cards through their actual unlock flow, not every inventory Item. If a recipe is missing, check party access, learned unlocks, category filter and the saved definition before creating duplicate recipes.

articles.title: Recipe editor and classifications
articles.summary: Link ingredient/output Items and create reusable unlock cards.

sections.title: Recipe definition
paragraphs: New Recipe creates an editor entry. Name is its display label, Card artwork is its recipe/unlock art, Classification groups it and Description explains it. Drag ingredient Items into Ingredients and set each required Qty. Drag the crafted Item into Result and set Produces to its output count.

The recipe’s prose does not replace Item references or quantities. Removing an ingredient deletes its recipe reference; it does not delete the world Item. Delete Recipe removes that definition rather than deleting all crafted copies.

sections.title: Availability and cards
paragraphs: The recipe browser’s Party access checkbox controls visibility/crafting for party members who have that recipe unlocked. Existing unlocks are retained. Create Recipe Card creates the supported inventory unlock Item. Save Recipe commits definition edits.

Crafting classifications have reusable names/icons and sort entries for the browser. Category selection is not an ingredient multiplier. Search recipes narrows name, category or description without altering the definition.

articles.title: Eidolons, sequential unlocks and effects
articles.summary: Configure six artwork/effect slots and unlock them with the designated currency.

sections.title: Character slots
paragraphs: Eidolons unlock sequentially E1 through E6. Each slot has a title, effect text, artwork and crop/scale. Active state indicates its unlock. The GM’s Configure controls edit that slot; activation uses the designated currency Item and normal sequence checks.

Activation currency Item is a UUID/reference to the Item used for unlocks; one copy is consumed per unlock through the supported workflow. Viewing a slot or Check Eidolon Effects does not consume currency.

sections.title: Artwork layers
paragraphs: Eidolon Appearance configures the shared background, glass shards/overlays and related presentation. The background should be the underlying scene without duplicating glass fragments. E3 has its separate upper glass layer. Character slot artwork is independent of these shared masks and overlays.

Select Existing Eidolons supports the module’s existing-item workflow. Effects need their supported item/effect implementation; prose and a decorative image alone are not arbitrary JavaScript. Save and activation are different actions.

articles.title: Keyboard shortcuts and movable widgets
articles.summary: Open normal workflows quickly and arrange local controls.

sections.title: Shortcut settings
paragraphs: Keyboard shortcut configuration selects the actions and key combinations offered by the module. A shortcut opens the same supported workflow as its normal button; it does not bypass ownership, resource costs, combat restrictions or resolving locks.
Check conflicts with other Foundry bindings if a key appears unresponsive. Editing a binding changes input behavior, not a character’s configured Skill/Ultimate text or charge.

sections.title: Move and reopen
paragraphs: Use widget grips for movement and resize handles for scale. Avoid dragging an action face when intending to move its frame. Local layout can differ between players. Close hides the local widget; show actions in the rail/phone/GM Panel restore the display.
The manual uses / to focus search, Escape to clear its query or dismiss a tooltip/image, and Back to revisit navigation. These documentation controls do not trigger combat shortcuts.

articles.title: Blow Up Tatsuo visual effect
articles.summary: Choose the target player and configure the separate token overlay.

sections.title: Configure and place
paragraphs: The GM Panel’s Configure Animation opens this effect’s settings. Select the intended player/character targeting and media presentation, then save. Place Floating Button shows a movable local trigger. The script API can also show or trigger the configured effect.

Media scale, position and timing tune the displayed animation. These are distinct from enhanced-form token replacement and Ultimate splash art. Choosing a file or reading the preview does not cast a character’s ability.

sections.title: Trigger
paragraphs: Using the live button broadcasts the configured visual over the selected player’s character tokens. It is an intentionally configured effect; it is not an implicit HP damage operation just because its name says Blow Up.

If nothing appears, verify target player/Actor, tokens on the scene, image/video path and current effect configuration. Reposition the local launcher through its grip rather than changing token placement.

articles.title: Macros, optional code and integration API
articles.summary: Use supported entry points and keep prose separate from executable code.

sections.title: Public API
paragraphs: After module readiness, access game.modules.get("telys-star-rail-ultimates").api. Read-only getters inspect state; request/trigger/setter methods are live actions with their normal restrictions. The tooltip system never evaluates configured prose as JavaScript.

sections.title: Request an ability
paragraphs: requestSkill(actor), requestUltimate(actor) and requestTechnique(actor) follow ownership, readiness, costs and summoning. getConfig(actor) reads merged configuration; getUltimateCharge(actor) reads active-form readiness. Use these flows instead of manually setting charge to simulate a completed cast.

rows: Shared Punchline; spending can fail if unaffordable.
Energy changes under active-form/round-lock rules; direct award is GM-only.
Read regular/enhanced design and states; omitted form means active.
GM free-mode component switch; active form and resolving checks apply.
Reset progress or edit regular/enhanced design. Circular charge is edited in its GM interfaces.

sections.title: Ultimate code context
paragraphs: The optional Ultimate code field runs as an async function with actor, token, combat, combatantId, config, game, canvas, ui, foundry and Hooks. A missing scene/combat can mean token or combat is absent. Await mechanical changes. A returned string may supply chat text when its configured description is empty.

punchline has get/set/add/spend. talent and skillPoints also provide max. tsru.moduleId identifies this module; tsru.state.get(key, fallback), set(key, value) and unset(key) keep custom state on the Actor. tsru.specialAha(fixedPunchline) requests its special Aha flow. Skill and HP-cost description fields are not this code context.

sections.title: Other public tools
paragraphs: openGMPanel, openDMCombatMenu, openCombatHudDesigner, openAhaConfig, openSkillPointConfig, openTalentPointConfig, openTechniquePointConfig, openBreakAppearance, openElementManager and openPathManager open their named interfaces. openEidolonConfig, openEidolonEffectsBrowser, openLightConeGenerator, openCrafting, openRecipeManager and openCraftingClassifications open their tools.

showOrb(actor), showCombatPartyHud, showUltimateUI, showSkillUI, showTalentUI, showAllAbilityBubbles and showTalentPopup(actor) show widgets/text. refreshOrbs and refreshResourceHuds repaint existing state. getSelectedMainCharacter and setLocalMainCharacter(actorId) handle the local selection.

setTemporaryToughnessWeaknesses(target, elementIds), addTemporaryToughnessWeakness(target, elementId) and resetTemporaryToughnessWeaknesses(target) manage temporary weaknesses. resetCanvasToughness restores scene NPC Toughness. insertActionAdvanceTurn(combatantId) inserts an extra turn. showAhaButton, toggleAhaOrb, triggerAhaInstant, triggerSpecialAha(actor, fixedPunchline), showBlowUpTatsuoButton and triggerBlowUpTatsuo operate their named systems. showSplash(options) is a local visual presentation call, not an Ultimate cast.

articles.title: Troubleshooting by symptom
articles.summary: Check active state, eligibility and assets before replacing configuration.

rows: Alternate orb did not replace Energy
Active form’s Standard/Alternate toggle, saved components and installed version.
Enabled system, active charge, ownership and resolving lock.
Correct active-form text/code fields and normal activation path; inspect reported script errors.
Active-form splash slot, accessible path and image preload/load result.
Current temporary participant and its matching completion button.
Active alternate mode and Pause Energy after Ultimate round lock.
Eligible Joyseeker, effective threshold roll, Aha event, active GM and installed version.
Full footprint within radius/bounds, occupancy and lighting barriers.
Connected GM, owner permissions, source Actor and saved choice/count.
Companion addon enabled and installed version’s Path/eligibility rules.
Valid linked Actor supplies live HP; edit that Actor.
Memosprite preview active but no token
Preview summoned is a designer state; use the actual summon action.
Visibility switch, frame/part offsets, scale and saved design.

sections.title: Menus, search and updates
paragraphs: Clear a search and choose All menus before assuming a setting was removed. Check the selected phone/Actor profile and active enhanced stance. A missing optional editor can require a compatible addon.

After an update, confirm the installed module version and reload the world/clients. A cached old module manifest or old browser script can leave new controls unavailable. If the manual reports a missing docs file, verify that the release ZIP includes docs/ and retry; hovering help must never be used as a substitute for missing module files.

articles.title: Glossary and common abbreviations
articles.summary: Distinguish the module’s similarly named resources and states.

rows: Character’s stored charge for a standard Ultimate.
Energy Regen ability score and its D&D-style modifier.
Shared Skill Point pool; separate from an individual Skill’s cost.
Shared resource for Techniques outside initiative.
Actor-specific combat pool with trigger and overcap limits.
Shared Elation resource associated with Aha.
The companion’s independent counter, dots or percentage.
Normal or Enhanced stance selecting the applicable kit.
Custom components replacing Energy charging for the active form.
GM independently switches each component on/off.
A number lights a cumulative ordered sequence.
Drawing order / charge order; independent concepts.
Designer display state, rather than a live cast or resource payment.
Map width/height inherited from an Actor’s prototype token.
Stable reference to an existing Actor or Item document.
Live amount / capacity or threshold, depending on the named resource.

articles.title: Complete field and control reference
articles.summary: Search individual settings and read their meanings, options and limits.

sections.title: Read a field entry
paragraphs: Each reference identifies its interface and human-readable label. Its description explains what it changes; numeric limits and dropdown choices appear when defined by the control. The optional identifier helps distinguish similarly named values and supports exact-name searching.
A maximum supplied by another setting is described as a configured limit. Current Energy, current HP and the shared SP balance are not interchangeable merely because each has a Current field.

sections.title: Read-only help and live actions
paragraphs: The same descriptions are used by hover help and searchable reference cards. New rows and refreshed panels receive help on rendering. Hovering, focusing or reading the manual does not save a field, spend a point, send a message, cast or advance a turn.

Use live buttons deliberately and draft editors’ Save actions when required. A picture, crop, font or color usually affects display; charge, HP cost, weakness, phase and turn controls affect mechanics. Search and contextual guide links connect the fields to their complete workflow.
